Story file: - docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md defines deep requirement validation (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-ERROR).
Rule implementation: - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - Header JSDoc ties this rule directly to the story: - @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-PATH - REQ-DEEP-PARSE / REQ-DEEP-FORMAT / REQ-DEEP-SECTION: - loadAndCacheRequirements(): - Reads story file via fs.readFileSync(resolvedStoryPath, "utf8"). - Uses regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g over the entire markdown to find all requirement IDs, regardless of section or list style. - Stores IDs in reqCache: Map<string, Set> keyed by resolved story path. - REQ-DEEP-CACHE: - reqCache is created once per Program in programListener() and passed through all helpers. - loadAndCacheRequirements() populates the cache on first access per file and reuses it thereafter. - REQ-DEEP-MATCH: - validateReqLine(): extracts reqId from a "@req" line, resolves the story (resolveStoryAndRequirements), then calls checkRequirementExists() to see if reqSet.has(reqId); if not, reports messageId "reqMissing" with { reqId, storyPath }. - validateImplementsLine(): parses "@supports " lines (parseImplementsLine), resolves story and requirement set, then runs checkRequirementExists() for each reqId on the line. - REQ-DEEP-PATH / Error Handling: - validateAndResolveStoryPath(): rejects any storyPath containing ".." or any absolute path (path.isAbsolute), and ensures resolved path stays within cwd. Invalid paths trigger context.report({ messageId: "invalidPath", data: { storyPath } }). - File read errors in loadAndCacheRequirements() are caught; in that case an empty Set is cached, so the rule degrades to reporting missing requirements rather than throwing. - REQ-DEEP-ERROR / User Experience: - meta.messages.reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'". - meta.messages.invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'". - Both messages include contextual data (reqId, storyPath) and are documented in JSDoc as satisfying REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC / REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT / REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY. - Integration with existing logic: - programListener(context) obtains sourceCode via context.getSourceCode() and iterates all comments (getAllComments), processing @story/@req/@supports within existing annotation style.
Plugin integration: - src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "valid-req-reference", so the rule is dynamically loaded from ./rules/valid-req-reference. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/valid-req-reference" to "error". - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() and configs.recommended/strict include this rule, ensuring it runs alongside existing annotation and file validation rules.

traceability.notes:
All key aspects of story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: Implemented via src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts and validated in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts. The rule reads actual story markdown files, extracts requirement IDs, and enforces that every @req and every ID listed after @supports exists in the corresponding story file.
- Quality Standards (formats & structures): The implementation uses a generic REQ-* regex across the full file content, which is proven in tests to work for standard story requirements, bullet-list requirements (story_bullet.md), and multi-story fixtures (story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md). Because it is section-agnostic and content-wide, it implicitly handles different story structures and sections.
- Integration: The rule is dynamically loaded with other rules in src/index.ts and is enabled at severity "error" in both recommended and strict flat configs, ensuring it works in concert with existing annotation-format and file-existence validation rules.
- User Experience: Error messages are clear and contextual—"Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" and "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'"—and tests assert not only the messageId but also the data, matching the story’s requirement for specific, consistent diagnostics.
- Error Handling: Invalid paths (path traversal, absolute paths, escaping project root) are caught and reported via invalidPath. File read errors are caught in loadAndCacheRequirements(), preventing crashes. Missing or malformed content simply yields an empty requirement set and results in reqMissing diagnostics rather than runtime failures.
- Documentation: The user-facing rule doc docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md explains the deep validation behavior, supported usage patterns, and error cases with concrete examples, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
Some advanced considerations in the story (e.g., configurable regex patterns, timestamp-based cache invalidation) are presented as implementation notes rather than strict requirements. The implemented behavior fully satisfies the explicit acceptance criteria and named REQ-* items. Therefore the story is fully implemented and passes.
